_schema: qa/typed/review.json v2: certification of decision-model gold labels. status=reviewed requires EVERY scenario in the label source covered by a style entry whose labels_sha256 matches the label source bytes, with reviewer named and rationale_ok true. Each entry records the batch and, for rows two blind annotators labelled, both verdicts; a disputed row carries its adjudicated label and the adjudicator's reason. `rubric_sha256` pins the annotation rubric the verdicts were made under. The reviewer field records WHO reviewed (a human expert, or a model review pass with its identity stated); human expert sign-off, when performed, is listed in `human_review`. tacit_calibrate.py refuses to recommend a floor until this ledger certifies the label source.
method: Two blind annotators per row under qa/typed/style-rubric.md with opaque row ids; Cohen's kappa recorded per batch; every disagreement adjudicated in writing. 2026-11 style-label gap: 4 train batches (raw agreement 0.979-0.993, kappa 0.978-0.993) and 2 holdout batches (0.981 and 1.000), plus a 30-row gold calibration (raw 0.90, kappa 0.863, gold accuracy 0.70 per annotator). The 169 pre-existing labels are carried at their 2026-11 audit verdicts, unchanged.

human_review.scope: audit sheet of 47 rows sampled across all 36 served labels (data/style-gap/human-audit/review-sheet.jsonl), each row's state shown with its proposed label; the reviewer accepted the labels as recorded
human_review.not_reviewed: row-by-row review of all 857 labels was not performed; the accept covers the sampled sheet, and the two-blind-annotator pass plus adjudication remains the per-row evidence
human_review.note: Recorded at the reviewer's instruction. The ledger's per-row reviewer field still names the model annotation pass; this block records the human expert acceptance of the sampled audit, not a claim that a human labelled or checked every row.

style.label: model-view-controller
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to model-view-controller: one behaviour (widget state plus event handling) is shared by two presentations that each render their own markup, which is a model/controller split with a view per shell. presentation-abstraction-control would need a hierarchy of cooperating presentation, abstraction and control agents per UI unit, and only the two shells are distinct presentations here. Recorded as a rubric tension: the authoring brief asked for edge-computing and neither annotator found placement near the data source load-bearing, so this row does not evidence its planned style.

style.label: monolithic
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to monolithic: the described system is one deployable - a single Ktor application, one artifact, whole-process restart, and explicitly no per-charger process to scale separately. Per-charger isolated state with one-message-at-a-time handling is the change the decision asks for, and the rubric labels the system described rather than the refactor requested; actor-based would require that isolation to already be the structure. Clarification worth carrying: a proposed redesign must not become the label.

style.label: hybrid-cloud
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to hybrid-cloud: machine control runs on servers the operator owns inside the terminal while booking, invoicing and notifications run in one public cloud region, and the split is load-bearing for both the 30 ms budget and offline operation. edge-computing would place the work on infrastructure the operator does not schedule; these are the operator's own on-premises servers.

style.label: actor-based
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to actor-based: the described mechanism is a worker per partner holding private tree state, receiving members as messages, answering one at a time, and restarted by a supervisor with the tree reloaded. The rule tree is the data those workers process with a hand-written matcher; rule-based-system would require an engine evaluating authored rules over a fact base, which nothing here describes.

style.label: broker
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to broker: one central hub that the element, inventory and billing programs all subscribe into is the described structure, and the shape translation happens inside the element program rather than in the backbone. enterprise-service-bus would require the mediation tier itself to translate between heterogeneous systems, which is the requested change, not the stated topology.

style.label: none
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to none: the described system is one nine-hundred-line routine inside a single coroutine with no deployment, no runtime topology and no inter-component boundary. The staged pipeline of resident coroutines is the redesign the decision asks for, and clarification 4 forbids labelling the requested change. Recorded finding: this row's authoring brief asked for actor-based, so the row does not evidence its planned style.

style.label: api-gateway
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to api-gateway: the estate's client surface is one edge that authenticates retail partners, applies per-partner quotas and routes into the ledger service, and the queue plus its four workers sit behind that entry point. The end-of-work signal is the requested change inside the ledger; event-driven would require the queue to be the system's coordination medium across components, which the text does not describe.

style.label: edge-computing
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to edge-computing: two thousand two hundred site controllers accumulate and cut batches locally and push them over metered, sometimes-lost links, so computation sits at the site and the link is the design constraint. The completeness marker is the requested change; none was the competing reading because the decision is wire reassembly, but step one finds a described runtime with an inter-component boundary.

style.label: reflection-architecture
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to reflection-architecture: the described mechanism is a runtime that inspects its own assemblies at start-up, discovers the declared converters, validators and serializers and adapts its processing chain to exactly that set. The third-party registry is the requested change, and microkernel-plugin would need a minimal core extended by plug-ins for most of its capabilities, which the text does not describe.

style.label: monolithic
style.adjudication: Adjudicated to monolithic: the described system is one Go binary with one database, released and restarted as a whole, behind one thin proxy that forwards to a single upstream. The director's rule language is a decision inside that deployable and its evaluation is a hand-written switch rather than an engine matching a fact base, so rule-based-system would label a mechanism the system does not have.
